thread:
taylan: Hey, heads up — we got reports of users flipping between canary and stable mid-session when hitting the EU edge. Seems tied to geo-redirect responses setting X-Region-Override header.
simi: Wait, flipping sessions? Like session stickiness lost?
jonathan: Seen similar behavior in staging last week when the proxy rewrote a header that we hash on. Could be hashing key change.
taylan: Repro steps from support:
- User lands on /signup -> routed to stable
- Redirect to /eu/ via our CDN -> response sets X-Region-Override: eu-west
- Next request goes to canary
simi: Oof. We use header fallback hashing order: cookie > header(client-region) > client-ip. If CDN adds X-Region-Override, that might bump it.
jonathan: Can you paste the request/response headers from the trace?
taylan: Sure:

```
GET /signup
Host: app.example
Cookie: _rid=abc123
X-Forwarded-For: 35.224.1.12

HTTP/1.1 302 Found
Location: /eu/
X-Region-Override: eu-west-1
```

After that, subsequent requests include X-Region-Override and our routing policy uses header precedence for geo.
deploy-bot: rollout/traffic-split check completed: canary=10% stable=90% — no errors
ops-sre: Is the cookie _rid stable across the redirect? If CDN strips cookies we lose stickiness.
simi: Good call. CDN was configured to strip some headers on redirect. We were relying on cookie, but lost it on the 302 because of SameSite mismatch.
jonathan: So two contributors: header injected by CDN which our hash picks up, plus cookie drop. The hash function uses a canonicalization step that normalizes header keys to lowercase and prefers region header if present.
taylan: Quick mitigation idea: change guard policy to pin by cookie if present, do not fall back to any header injected by intermediaries. Add 'trusted-headers' whitelist.
simi: Agree. Also add a short-term telemetry alert to detect user ids shifting buckets within 30s. We can query traces with:

```
SELECT user_id, ARRAY_AGG(DISTINCT route) as routes
FROM request_logs
WHERE time > now() - interval '1 hour'
GROUP BY user_id
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT route) > 1
LIMIT 20;
```

jonathan: Can you toggle the guard ordering in console? I can push a quick patch to the hash key computation.
ops-sre: ETA for guard ordering change? Need to coordinate with oncall for a config rollout.
taylan: I'll open a canary-only config that whitelists 'Cookie' as primary key and disables header fallbacks. Patch: 

```
rollout.guards.hash_order = ["cookie", "client_ip"]
rollout.guards.trusted_headers = ["x-forwarded-for"]
```

Will roll to 5% internal users first.
simi: Also add a QA check to simulate CDN redirect preserving cookie vs dropping it.
deploy-bot: config-rollout started: id=cfg-2026-1893 target=internal-5% :rocket:
jonathan: After we confirm, add console UX note so customers can opt-in to 'trust intermediary headers' if they know their CDN behavior.
taylan: Filed ENG-1298 (investigate CDN header injection + sticky sessions). I'll monitor telemetry and post results.
ops-sre: For immediate troubleshooting, adding a temporary header-strip on edge that removes X-Region-Override might help while we fix guards.
simi: Can we also add a regression test in eng-runtime that asserts hash(key) invariant across automated redirects? E.g., simulate 302 chain and ensure same routing outcome.
jonathan: Yup, I'll add a unit + integration test in routing spec.
taylan: Thanks. I'll update this thread with the rollback token and telemetry snapshots. :eyes:
simi: :thumbsup:
